description: An introduction to matter, its three states, the arrangement and behaviour of particles, changes of state, and the difference between physical and chemical changes.

options.text: Anything that has mass and occupies space
Anything that can be seen only

mcq.explanation: Matter has two defining properties: it has mass and it takes up space or volume. Exam Tip: Air has mass and occupies space, so it IS matter even though invisible. The test is mass plus space, not visibility.

mcq.questionText: The three states of matter are:
mcq.explanation: Matter exists in three common physical states: solid, liquid and gas. Exam Tip: They differ in how tightly particles are packed, from solid which is tightest to gas which is loosest.

mcq.questionText: In which state of matter are the particles packed most closely together and fixed in position?
mcq.explanation: Closely packed, fixed particles give a definite shape, which is a solid. Exam Tip: Solid has fixed shape and volume; liquid has fixed volume but takes the shape of its container; gas has neither fixed.

mcq.questionText: The change of state from solid directly to gas without passing through the liquid state is called:
mcq.explanation: Skipping the liquid state and going straight from solid to gas is sublimation. Exam Tip: Iodine and dry ice sublime. It is solid to gas directly.

mcq.questionText: The change of state from liquid to solid is called:
mcq.explanation: A liquid becoming solid loses heat, which is freezing or solidification. Exam Tip: Freezing is the reverse of melting. Water freezes to ice at 0 C.

mcq.questionText: The change of state from liquid to gas is called:
mcq.explanation: A liquid gaining heat becomes gas through evaporation, or boiling at the boiling point. Exam Tip: Evaporation happens at the surface at any temperature; boiling happens throughout the liquid at the boiling point.

mcq.questionText: The change of state from gas to liquid is called:
mcq.explanation: A gas losing heat forms a liquid through condensation. Exam Tip: Condensation is the reverse of evaporation, such as water droplets forming on a cold glass.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a PHYSICAL change?
mcq.explanation: Melting ice gives water, the same substance, and it is reversible, so a physical change forms no new substance. Exam Tip: A physical change means no new substance is formed, such as melting, dissolving or boiling.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a CHEMICAL change?
mcq.explanation: Burning charcoal produces ash and gases, which are new substances. Exam Tip: Signs of a chemical change include a new substance, colour change, gas released, heat or light given off, and being hard to reverse.

mcq.questionText: Rusting of iron is an example of a chemical change because:

options.text: The iron can easily be turned back

mcq.explanation: Iron reacts with oxygen and water to form a new substance, rust, which is iron oxide. Exam Tip: Forming a new substance is the key sign of a chemical change.

mcq.questionText: Which property is true of a gas?

options.text: It has a fixed shape and fixed volume
It has no fixed shape and no fixed volume
It has a fixed volume but no fixed shape

mcq.explanation: Gas particles are far apart and move freely, filling any container. Exam Tip: Gas has no fixed shape or volume and is easily compressed. Liquid has fixed volume but no fixed shape. Solid has both fixed.

mcq.questionText: When water is heated and turns into steam, this change is:

options.text: A chemical change because a new substance forms
A physical change because it can be reversed to water

mcq.explanation: Steam is still water, H2O, in gas form; cooling turns it back, so no new substance is formed. Exam Tip: State changes are physical because the substance stays chemically the same.

mcq.questionText: The process by which particles of a substance spread and mix on their own, such as perfume filling a room, is called:
mcq.explanation: Particles moving from where they are many to where they are few is diffusion. Exam Tip: Diffusion is fastest in gases and shows that matter is made of moving particles.

mcq.questionText: Which change of state takes place when candle wax becomes liquid as the candle burns?
mcq.explanation: Solid wax gains heat and becomes liquid, which is melting. Exam Tip: A candle shows BOTH the wax melting, which is physical, and the wick burning, which is chemical.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following best shows that a chemical change has occurred?

options.text: Formation of a new substance with different properties

mcq.explanation: A new substance with new properties is formed. Exam Tip: Shape and size changes are physical. A NEW substance is the mark of a chemical change.

fib.questionText: Matter is anything that has mass and occupies __________.
fib.explanation: Matter must have mass and take up space, so it occupies space or volume. Exam Tip: Mass plus space equals matter. Both must be present.

fib.questionText: The change of state from solid to liquid is called __________.
fib.explanation: A solid gaining heat becomes a liquid, which is melting. Exam Tip: Melting point example: ice melts at 0 C.

fib.questionText: The change of state from gas to liquid is called __________.
fib.explanation: A gas losing heat turns into a liquid, which is condensation. Exam Tip: Condensation forms dew and droplets on a cold surface.

fib.questionText: A change in which a new substance is formed is called a __________ change.
fib.explanation: When a new substance is formed the change is chemical. Exam Tip: A chemical change gives a new substance and is usually irreversible.

fib.questionText: The direct change of a solid to a gas without becoming liquid is called __________.
fib.explanation: Going straight from solid to gas without a liquid stage is sublimation. Exam Tip: Iodine and dry ice sublime; the process skips the liquid stage.

fib.questionText: In a __________ change, no new substance is formed and the change can usually be reversed.
fib.explanation: A physical change forms no new substance and is usually reversible. Exam Tip: Melting, boiling, dissolving and magnetising are physical changes.

fib.questionText: The state of matter with a fixed volume but no fixed shape is __________.
fib.explanation: A liquid keeps its volume but takes the shape of its container. Exam Tip: Liquid has fixed volume but no fixed shape.

fib.questionText: The spreading of particles from a region of high concentration to a region of low concentration is called __________.
fib.explanation: Particles spreading from high to low concentration is diffusion. Exam Tip: Diffusion is evidence that matter is made of tiny moving particles.

fib.questionText: The burning of charcoal is an example of a __________ change.
fib.explanation: Burning charcoal forms new substances, so it is a chemical change. Exam Tip: Burning, which is combustion, is always a chemical change.

fib.questionText: The temperature at which a liquid changes to a gas throughout the liquid is called the __________ point.
fib.explanation: The temperature at which a liquid boils throughout is the boiling point. Exam Tip: Water boils at 100 C at sea level. Boiling occurs throughout while evaporation occurs only at the surface.

tf.questionText: Matter is anything that has mass and occupies space.
tf.explanation: Mass and occupying space are the two defining properties of matter. Exam Tip: Air qualifies as matter because it is invisible but has mass and takes up space.

tf.questionText: Melting is the change of state from liquid to solid.
tf.explanation: Melting is solid to liquid; liquid to solid is freezing. Exam Tip: The statement reverses melting and freezing. Melting equals solid to liquid.

tf.questionText: Burning of wood is a chemical change.
tf.explanation: Burning wood forms new substances such as ash and gases. Exam Tip: Combustion always forms new substances.

tf.questionText: In a solid, particles are far apart and move freely.
tf.explanation: In a solid the particles are closely packed and only vibrate in place. Exam Tip: Far apart and free describes a gas; solids are closely packed and only vibrate.

tf.questionText: Physical changes can usually be reversed.
tf.explanation: Physical changes form no new substance and can usually be reversed. Exam Tip: Reversible plus no new substance equals physical change.

tf.questionText: Sublimation is the change of a solid directly into a gas.
tf.explanation: Sublimation is the direct change from solid to gas without a liquid stage. Exam Tip: Iodine and dry ice are classic examples.

tf.questionText: Rusting of iron is a physical change.
tf.explanation: Rusting forms a new substance, so it is a chemical change. Exam Tip: Rusting is chemical because iron plus oxygen plus water gives rust.

tf.questionText: A gas has neither a fixed shape nor a fixed volume.
tf.explanation: Gas particles move freely and fill any container, so a gas has no fixed shape or volume. Exam Tip: Gas has no fixed shape or volume and is easily compressed.

tf.questionText: Dissolving sugar in water is a chemical change.
tf.explanation: Dissolving forms no new substance and can be reversed, so it is physical. Exam Tip: Dissolving is physical because sugar can be recovered by evaporating the water.

tf.questionText: Condensation and evaporation are reverse processes.
tf.explanation: Evaporation is liquid to gas and condensation is gas to liquid, so they are opposite processes. Exam Tip: Evaporation is liquid to gas; condensation is gas to liquid.

summary.correctAnswer: Anything that has mass and occupies space (has volume).
summary.explanation: Even invisible things like air are matter because they have mass and take up space. Exam Tip: The test for matter is mass plus space, not whether it can be seen.

summary.correctAnswer: The solid, liquid and gas forms in which matter can exist.
summary.explanation: The three states differ mainly in how their particles are arranged and how freely they move. Exam Tip: Remember the order solid, liquid, gas from tightest to loosest packing.

summary.correctAnswer: How particles are packed: closely packed and fixed in solids, close but moving in liquids, and far apart and free in gases.
summary.explanation: The arrangement of particles explains the shape and volume of each state. Exam Tip: Solid particles only vibrate; gas particles move fast and fill the container.

summary.correctAnswer: The change of state from solid to liquid on gaining heat.
summary.explanation: At the melting point a solid absorbs heat and becomes a liquid. Exam Tip: Ice melts to water at 0 C.

summary.correctAnswer: The change of state from liquid to solid on losing heat.
summary.explanation: Freezing, also called solidification, is the reverse of melting. Exam Tip: Water freezes to ice at 0 C.

summary.correctAnswer: The change of state from liquid to gas; evaporation at the surface at any temperature and boiling throughout at the boiling point.
summary.explanation: Both turn a liquid into a gas but happen in different ways. Exam Tip: Water boils at 100 C at sea level, but evaporation can occur at any temperature.

summary.correctAnswer: The change of state from gas to liquid on losing heat.
summary.explanation: Condensation is the reverse of evaporation and forms droplets on cold surfaces. Exam Tip: Dew and misting on a cold glass are examples of condensation.

summary.correctAnswer: The change of state from solid directly to gas without becoming a liquid.
summary.explanation: Sublimation skips the liquid stage entirely. Exam Tip: Iodine and dry ice sublime, and it is used to purify iodine.

summary.correctAnswer: A change in which no new substance is formed and which can usually be reversed.
summary.explanation: Only the appearance or state changes, not the substance itself. Exam Tip: Melting, boiling, dissolving and magnetising are physical changes.

summary.correctAnswer: A change in which one or more new substances are formed and which is usually irreversible.
summary.explanation: New substances with different properties are produced during a chemical change. Exam Tip: Signs include a new substance, colour change, gas, heat or light, and being hard to reverse.

hoq.questionText: A burning candle shows two changes at the same time: the solid wax near the flame turns to liquid, and the wick burns giving light and smoke. Classify the two changes correctly.

options.text: Melting of wax is physical; burning of the wick is chemical
Melting of wax is chemical; burning of the wick is physical

hoq.explanation: The wax melting is solid to liquid, reversible and forms no new substance, so it is physical. The wick burning gives smoke and gases and is not reversible, so it is chemical. Exam Tip: A single event can contain BOTH types of change. Test each part by asking whether a new substance is formed.

hoq.questionText: A student is given four processes: (i) ice melting, (ii) milk turning sour, (iii) water boiling, (iv) a nail rusting. Which processes are physical and which are chemical?
hoq.explanation: Ice melting and water boiling are state changes of water, so they are physical. Milk souring involves acids and rusting forms a new substance, so both are chemical. Exam Tip: Ask whether you can get the original back easily; yes points to physical and no points to chemical.

hoq.questionText: A student places purple iodine crystals in a beaker and warms them gently. Purple vapour rises and, on touching a cool surface, purple solid forms again, with no liquid seen at any stage. Name the two changes and state whether the overall process is physical or chemical.
hoq.explanation: Solid iodine turns directly into vapour, which is sublimation, then the vapour turns back to solid on the cool surface, which is deposition. The iodine stays iodine with no new substance, so the process is physical. Exam Tip: No liquid seen at any stage rules out melting and boiling and points to sublimation and deposition. Sublimation is used to purify iodine.
